1. Wish to be dead
Subject endorses thoughts about a wish to be dead or not alive anymore, or a wish to fall asleep
and not wake up.
2. Non-specific Active Suicidal Thoughts
General non-specific thoughts of wanting to end one's life / commit suicide (e.g. "I've thought
plan during the assessment period.
3. Active Suicidal Ideation with Any Methods (Not Plan) Without Intent to Act
Subject endorses thoughts of suicide and has thought of at least one method during the
assessment period. This is different from a specific plan with time, place or method details
worked out (e.g. thought of method to kill self but not a specific plan). Includes person who
where or how I would actually do it… and I would never go through with it".
4. Active Suicidal Ideation with Some Intent to Act, without Specific Plan
Active suicidal thoughts of killing oneself and subject reports having some intent to act on such
thoughts, as opposed to "I have the thoughts but I definitely will not do anything about them".
5. Active Suicidal Ideation with Specific Plan and Intent
Thoughts of killing oneself with details of plan fully or partially worked out and subject has
some intent to carry it out.
(Have you started to work out or worked out the details of how to kill yourself? Do you intend
to carry out this plan?)
Most Severe Ideation
The following feature should be rated with respect to the most severe type of ideation (i.e. 1-5
from above, with 1 being the least severe and 5 being the most severe). Ask about time he/she
was feeling the most suicidal.
Description of Ideation
Controllability
(Are there things - anyone or anything (e.g. family, religion, pain of death) - that stopped you
from wanting to die or acting on thoughts of committing suicide?)
Reasons for Ideation
(What sort of reasons did you have for thinking about wanting to die or killing yourself? Was it
to end the pain or stop the way you were feeling (in other words you couldn't go on living with
this pain or how you were feeling) or was it to get attention, revenge or a reaction from others? Or both?)
Actual Attempt (Since Last Visit)
A potentially self-injurious act committed with at least some wish to die, as a result of act. Behaviour was in part thought of as method to kill oneself. Intent does not have to be 100%. If
there is any intent/desire to die associated with the act, then it can be considered an actual
harm. If person pulls trigger while gun is in mouth but gun is broken so no injury results, this is
considered an attempt. Inferring Intent: Even if an individual denies intent/wish to die, it may be inferred clinically from
the behaviour or circumstances. For example, a highly lethal act that is clearly not an accident
so no other intent but suicide can be inferred (e.g. gunshot to head, jumping from window of a
high floor/storey). Also, if someone denies intent to die, but they thought that what they did
could be lethal, intent
maybe inferred.

(Have you made a suicide attempt? Have you done anything to harm yourself? Have you done anything dangerous where you could have died?  (What did you do?  Did you ___ as a way to end your life?  Did you want to die (even a little) when you___?  Were you
trying to end your life when you___?  Or did you think it was possible you could have died
from___?) Or did you do it purely for other reasons / without ANY intention of killing yourself (like to
relieve stress, feel better, get sympathy, or get something else to happen)? (Self-Injurious Behaviour without suicidal intent))

Has subject engaged in Non-Suicidal Self-Injurious Behaviour (Since Last Visit)
Interrupted Attempt (Since Last Visit)
When the person is interrupted (by an outside circumstance) from starting the potentially self-
injurious act (if not for that, actual attempt would have occurred). Overdose: Person has pills in hand but is stopped from ingesting. Once they ingest any pills, this
becomes an attempt rather than an interrupted attempt. Shooting: Person has gun pointed
towards self, gun is taken away by someone else, or he/she is somehow prevented from pulling
trigger. Once they pull the trigger, even if the gun fails to fire, it is an attempt. Jumping: Person
is poised to jump, is grabbed and taken down from ledge. Hanging: Person has noose around
neck but has not yet started to hang - is stopped from doing so.

Aborted Attempt (Since Last Visit)
When person begins to take steps towards making a suicide attempt, but stops themselves
before they actually have engaged in any self-destructive behaviour. Examples are similar to
interrupted attempts, except that the individual stops him/herself instead of being stopped by
something else.
(Has there been a time when you started to do something to try to end your life but you
stopped yourself before you actually did anything?)

Inclusion 2. BMI from 18.0 to 32.0 kg/m2 (inclusive).
a) Medical history
b) Physical examination
c) Neurological examination

b) Will remain abstinent during the trial and for 90 days plus 5 half-lives (ie, 92 days) after the
last dose of IMP.
d) Have had a bilateral orchiectomy.
Inclusion 5. Female participants who are surgically sterile (ie, have undergone bilateral
oophorectomy or hysterectomy) or who have been postmenopausal for at least 12 consecutive
months. This will be confirmed with a follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) assessment.
Inclusion 6. Ability to provide written, informed consent prior to initiation of any trial-related
procedures, and ability, in the opinion of the principal investigator, to comply with all the
requirements of the trial.
Exclusion 1. Non-English speakers and those with language or hearing impairments will not
participate in the trial.
Exclusion 2. Participants who are breast-feeding and/or who have a positive pregnancy test
result prior to receiving the IMP.
Exclusion 3. Clinically significant abnormality in past medical history, or at the screening
physical examination, that in the investigators or sponsor’s opinion may place the participant at
immunologic disease.
Exclusion 4. History of drug and/or alcohol abuse within 2 years prior to screening.
Exclusion 5. History of or current hepatitis or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome or carriers
of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and/or hepatitis C antibodies (anti-HCV), or human
immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibodies. Exceptions are permitted for participants with a prior
history of infection with hepatitis A who have fully recovered and are experiencing no liver
sequelae, or with hepatitis C who have been adequately treated to be considered cured with no
liver sequelae.
Exclusion 6. History of any significant drug allergy or known or suspected hypersensitivity to any
component of IMP.
Exclusion 7. A positive urine or breath alcohol test or urine drug screen for substances of abuse
at screening or upon check-in to the trial site.
Exclusion 8. Any history of significant bleeding or hemorrhagic tendencies.
Exclusion 9. A history of difficulty in donating blood.
Exclusion 10. The donation of blood or plasma within 30 days prior to the first dose of IMP.
Exclusion 11. Participants having taken an investigational drug within 90 days prior to first dose.
Exclusion 12. Use of prescription, over-the-counter, herbal medications, or vitamin supplements
within 14 days prior to the first dose of IMP and oral antibiotics within 30 days prior to the first
dose of IMP. The sponsor may allow exceptions only if the medication’s administration is
deemed unlikely to impact the PK result.
Exclusion 13. Exposure to any substances known to stimulate hepatic microsomal enzymes
etc).
Exclusion 14. Use of tobacco products or daily exposure to second-hand smoke within 2 months
prior to the screening visit, or urine cotinine concentrations >200 ng/mL or serum cotinine
concentrations >20 ng/mL at screening or check-in.
Exclusion 15. Participants presenting with, or having a history of, uncontrolled hypertension
(systolic blood pressure [SBP] >140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure [DBP] >90 mmHg in the
supine position) or symptomatic hypotension or orthostatic hypotension, which is defined as a
decrease of ≥20 mmHg in SBP and/or a decrease of ≥10 mmHg in DBP after at least 3 minutes of
standing compared with the previous supine blood pressure, at screening or check-in.

Exclusion 17. History of unexplained syncope.
Exclusion 18. Abnormal ECG findings at screening or check-in including QT interval corrected for
heart rate using Fridericia’s formula (QTcF) >450 msec for male participants or >470 msec for
female participants, QRS interval >120 msec, or PR interval >200 msec.
Exclusion 19. Personal or family history of sudden death or long QT syndrome.
Exclusion 20. History of serious mental disorders that, in the opinion of the investigator, would
exclude the participant from participating in this trial.
Exclusion 21. Participants with no permanent place of residence.
Exclusion 22. Any participant who, in the opinion of the investigator, should not participate in
the trial.
Exclusion 23. Previous exposure to OPC-224333.
Exclusion 24. Consumption of alcohol and/or food and beverages containing methylxanthines
grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, Seville orange juice, blueberry juice, or cranberry juice within 72 hours prior to dosing.
Exclusion 25. Participants with active suicidal ideation or suicidal behavior within the last 6
months, at the screening visit (Baseline/Screening version), and/or prior to dosing (as
evidenced by clinical examination or an answer of “yes” on Questions 4 or 5 of the C SSRS Since Last Visit version) or suicidal behavior is present in the C-SSRS.
Exclusion 26. Not able to consume the FDA HFM (High Fat Meal) for Part 2 and Part 3 within 20
minutes.
Exclusion 27. Participant has any significant primary sleep disorder. Participants with known
untreated moderate or severe sleep apnea, other major untreated sleep disorders, or a known
diagnosis of a circadian rhythm disorder. Participants adequately treated for obstructive sleep
apnea are not excluded.
Exclusion 28. Participants with abnormal liver function and or hepatic impairment, defined as
participants with aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), or alkaline
phosphatase > the upper limit of normal (ULN) or total bilirubin > the ULN.

field_name: A potentially self-injurious act committed with at least some wish to die, as a result of act. Behaviour was in part thought of as method to kill oneself. Intent does not have to be 100%. If

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: there is any intent/desire to die associated with the act, then it can be considered an actual

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: harm. If person pulls trigger while gun is in mouth but gun is broken so no injury results, this is

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: considered an attempt. Inferring Intent: Even if an individual denies intent/wish to die, it may be inferred clinically from

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: the behaviour or circumstances. For example, a highly lethal act that is clearly not an accident

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: so no other intent but suicide can be inferred (e.g. gunshot to head, jumping from window of a

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: high floor/storey). Also, if someone denies intent to die, but they thought that what they did

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: could be lethal, intent

form_name: QSC302573, 05c - Period 3 Parts 1 and 2 Draft v0.1
field_name: maybe inferred.

1. Wish to be dead
Subject endorses thoughts about a wish to be dead or not alive anymore, or a wish to fall asleep
and not wake up.
2. Non-specific Active Suicidal Thoughts
General non-specific thoughts of wanting to end one's life / commit suicide (e.g. "I've thought
plan during the assessment period.
3. Active Suicidal Ideation with Any Methods (Not Plan) Without Intent to Act
Subject endorses thoughts of suicide and has thought of at least one method during the
assessment period. This is different from a specific plan with time, place or method details
worked out (e.g. thought of method to kill self but not a specific plan). Includes person who
where or how I would actually do it… and I would never go through with it".
4. Active Suicidal Ideation with Some Intent to Act, without Specific Plan
Active suicidal thoughts of killing oneself and subject reports having some intent to act on such
thoughts, as opposed to "I have the thoughts but I definitely will not do anything about them".
5. Active Suicidal Ideation with Specific Plan and Intent
Thoughts of killing oneself with details of plan fully or partially worked out and subject has
some intent to carry it out.
(Have you started to work out or worked out the details of how to kill yourself? Do you intend
to carry out this plan?)
Most Severe Ideation
The following feature should be rated with respect to the most severe type of ideation (i.e. 1-5
from above, with 1 being the least severe and 5 being the most severe). Ask about time he/she
was feeling the most suicidal.
Controllability
(Are there things - anyone or anything (e.g. family, religion, pain of death) - that stopped you

Reasons for Ideation
(What sort of reasons did you have for thinking about wanting to die or killing yourself? Was it
to end the pain or stop the way you were feeling (in other words you couldn't go on living with
this pain or how you were feeling) or was it to get attention, revenge or a reaction from others? Or both?)
Actual Attempt (Since Last Visit)
A potentially self-injurious act committed with at least some wish to die, as a result of act. Behaviour was in part thought of as method to kill oneself. Intent does not have to be 100%. If
there is any intent/desire to die associated with the act, then it can be considered an actual
harm. If person pulls trigger while gun is in mouth but gun is broken so no injury results, this is
considered an attempt. Inferring Intent: Even if an individual denies intent/wish to die, it may be inferred clinically from
the behaviour or circumstances. For example, a highly lethal act that is clearly not an accident
so no other intent but suicide can be inferred (e.g. gunshot to head, jumping from window of a
high floor/storey). Also, if someone denies intent to die, but they thought that what they did
could be lethal, intent
maybe inferred.

When the person is interrupted (by an outside circumstance) from starting the potentially self-

towards self, gun is taken away by someone else, or he/she is somehow prevented from pulling
trigger. Once they pull the trigger, even if the gun fails to fire, it is an attempt. Jumping: Person
is poised to jump, is grabbed and taken down from ledge. Hanging: Person has noose around
neck but has not yet started to hang - is stopped from doing so.
